documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 05/10/2026  Arrival 14:05, EMS trauma activation
Patient: Logan Fontaine, 29M

CC: SOB, chest pain after high-speed MVC

HPI: 29M, belted driver, high-speed collision this afternoon. Short of breath with chest pain. States he had not been drinking. Known to this hospital: April 2025 crash with esophageal rupture repaired by left thoracotomy; November 2025 crash with a blunt thoracic aortic injury treated with an endovascular stent graft.

PMH: esophageal rupture with pleural effusion (repaired 04/2025); blunt thoracic aortic injury (TEVAR 11/2025).
PSH: left thoracotomy 2025, TEVAR 2025, T&A as a child.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father HTN, mother hypothyroidism; no aortic, connective tissue or bleeding disorders.
SH: never smoker; social alcohol 1-2/wk; delivery driver.

Arrival VS: HR 110, RR 26, SpO2 89% RA.

Exam: tachypneic and tachycardic. Breath sounds decreased on the left with crepitus of subcutaneous emphysema over the left chest wall. Trachea midline. Heart regular, tachycardic. Abdomen soft.

ED course: CXR with a left pneumothorax. Left chest tube placed; saturation came up to 92%. Over the next few hours his work of breathing worsened and the drainage system showed a large air leak that did not let up. Repeat film: tube well placed, pneumothorax unchanged. A persistent large leak with a lung that won't re-expand raises concern for an airway injury. Thoracic surgery consulted, plan for bronchoscopy in the OR.

Impression:
1. Tracheobronchial rupture, suspected — persistent air leak and pneumothorax despite chest tube.
2. Blunt chest trauma, high-speed MVC.
3. Hx esophageal rupture (repaired) and blunt aortic injury s/p TEVAR.

Dispo: to OR with thoracic surgery 19:20.

events.reason: Left main bronchus tear after blunt chest trauma

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Left chest tube in place. Persistent left pneumothorax. Subcutaneous emphysema along the left chest wall. Thoracic aortic stent graft in expected position just beyond the left subclavian origin. Postsurgical changes of prior left thoracotomy and distal esophageal repair. Right lung clear. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. No fracture.
reports.conclusion: Persistent left pneumothorax despite chest tube; stent graft in expected position.

Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for pain

documents.title: Operative Report — Bronchoscopy and Left Thoracotomy, Bronchial Repair
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DEPARTMENT OF SURGERY, THORACIC
Date of operation: 05/10/2026

Preoperative diagnosis: Suspected left-sided tracheobronchial rupture after blunt chest trauma; persistent air leak and left pneumothorax despite tube thoracostomy.
Postoperative diagnosis: Tear of the left main bronchus.
Procedures: 1. Flexible bronchoscopy. 2. Redo left posterolateral thoracotomy with primary repair of the left main bronchus.
Anesthesia: General; bronchoscopy-guided placement of a right-sided double-lumen tube.
Allergies: NKDA.

Findings: Trachea and carina intact. Tear in the proximal left main bronchus. Right airways normal. At thoracotomy, adhesions from the prior operation; the bronchial tear confirmed and its edges healthy.

Description: Flexible bronchoscopy through the single-lumen tube defined the injury, then airway secured with the double-lumen tube under bronchoscopic guidance. Redo left thoracotomy through the prior incision. Adhesiolysis. Left main bronchus exposed; tear repaired primarily with interrupted absorbable sutures. Leak test under saline: no leak. Two left chest tubes. Closure in layers.

EBL modest. No complications. To SICU intubated, extubated the next morning.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/10/2026  Discharged 05/21/2026
Service: Thoracic Surgery

Principal diagnosis: Tracheobronchial rupture (left main bronchus tear) after blunt chest trauma, high-speed MVC.
Other: history of esophageal rupture repaired 04/2025; blunt thoracic aortic injury s/p TEVAR 11/2025.
Allergies: NKDA.

Course: 29M with a persistent large air leak and unresolved left pneumothorax after ED chest tube placement. CT chest showed the pneumothorax persisting with the tube in place and the aortic stent graft in expected position. Bronchoscopy in the OR on 5/10 showed a tear of the left main bronchus, repaired primarily through a redo left thoracotomy (see operative report). Extubated POD 1. Air leak stopped and the lung stayed up; chest tubes removed in stages. Subcutaneous emphysema resolved. Ambulating, eating a regular diet, pain controlled on oral medication.

Discharge medications:
- oxycodone 5 mg, 1 tab every 6 h as needed for severe pain, #20, no refills
- acetaminophen 500 mg, 2 tabs every 8 h as needed for pain

Activity: no lifting over 10 lb, no driving while taking oxycodone. Off work until cleared.
Follow-up: thoracic surgery clinic in about 3 weeks with chest x-ray; surveillance bronchoscopy at about 8 weeks. PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Outreach Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
TCM outreach, 1 business day after discharge (d/c 5/21, regional hospital, thoracic surgery).
Spoke with pt. Home with his mother staying for a few days. Has discharge paperwork and both prescriptions filled. Taking acetaminophen regularly and oxycodone at night. Breathing comfortably, no fever, incision dry. Reviewed reasons to call 911 or go to the ED: sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, fever, redness or drainage from the incision.
PCP visit booked Tue 5/26 at 1:40. Hospital records requested.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Records from the regional hospital in hand: ED record, op report, discharge summary.

29M, belted driver in a high-speed crash 5/10. In the ED: HR 110, RR 26, sat 89% on room air, left pneumothorax with subcutaneous emphysema; chest tube brought him to 92% at first, but a large air leak persisted and the lung stayed down. Bronchoscopy in the OR found a tear of the left main bronchus, repaired through a redo left thoracotomy the same night. Extubated POD 1. Home 5/21 on oxycodone and acetaminophen.

Today: mild soreness along the incision, worse when he turns in bed. Stopped the oxycodone two days ago. No shortness of breath walking around the neighborhood, no fever, no cough to speak of. Eating normally, no swallowing trouble. Mother has been helping out.

Weight 77 kg.

Exam: comfortable, conversational without effort. Lungs clear and equal. No crepitus. Heart regular, no murmur. Left thoracotomy incision healing, clean, no erythema; chest tube sites closed. Right groin from last fall unremarkable. No calf tenderness or edema.

A/P
1. Tracheobronchial rupture s/p primary repair of left main bronchus 5/10/26 — recovering well. Thoracic surgery visit with CXR 6/9; bronchoscopy planned around 8 weeks out. ED precautions reviewed.
2. Blunt chest trauma, post-op pain — acetaminophen as needed. Return unused oxycodone at the pharmacy take-back.
3. Blunt thoracic aortic injury s/p TEVAR — stent graft in expected position on the inpatient CT. One-year CTA with vascular surgery in November.
4. CBC today.
5. Off work until cleared by thoracic surgery; work note given.

TCM, high complexity. Contact made 5/22.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Postsurgical changes of left thoracotomy. Thoracic aortic stent graft in stable position. Left lung fully expanded. No pneumothorax. No pleural effusion. Right lung clear. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Left lung fully expanded; no pneumothorax or effusion.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — THORACIC SURGERY CLINIC
Visit 06/09/2026

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Fontaine returns a month after flexible bronchoscopy and redo left thoracotomy with primary repair of a left main bronchus tear (5/10/26). We also cared for him after his esophageal repair last year.

He is off opioids, walking daily, and denies dyspnea, cough, hemoptysis or fevers. Incision healed. Breath sounds equal bilaterally.
Chest radiograph today: left lung fully expanded, no pneumothorax or effusion.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: acetaminophen as needed.

Plan: surveillance bronchoscopy on 7/7/26 to look at the repair. Remains off work until then. Lifting limit of 10 lb continues.

Thoracic Surgery

documents.title: Bronchoscopy Report and Clinic Letter
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — THORACIC SURGERY / ENDOSCOPY
Date of procedure: 07/07/2026

Procedure: Flexible bronchoscopy under moderate sedation.
Indication: Surveillance after primary repair of a left main bronchus tear (5/10/2026).
Allergies: NKDA.

Findings: Normal vocal cords, trachea and carina. The left main bronchus repair is fully healed with a smooth, intact lining and a normal caliber; no narrowing, granulation tissue or suture exposure. Left upper and lower lobe airways normal. Right airways normal. Secretions minimal.

Impression: Healed left main bronchus repair without stenosis.

Plan: Cleared to return to work at full duty on 7/13/2026 with no restrictions. No routine thoracic surgery follow-up needed; we are glad to see him again for any new breathing symptoms.

Thoracic Surgery
